name: Launch a new paid creative test, start to finish
trigger: an approved card from Propose | on demand
human_role: Performance creative lead running one test from research to the first read
inputs_required: brand brain: voice, audience avatars, claim tiers, product facts
approved idea/card record with bottleneck and expected effect
registry: past creative tests and learnings for this persona and angle
metric contract: hook_rate, cvr_overall, cpa, roas_blended, with freshness stamps
Reference Scout access for competitor and swipe material

steps.name: Pull the objection map and format scan
steps.does: Pulls the brand's existing mined research (voice of customer, owned by the Brand Brain Keeper) plus a fresh check of the account's own last 90 days of ad-level results for which formats currently deliver best (hook rate, hold rate, CPA by format).
inputs: own account ad-level results, last 90 days
steps.output: objection map (each objection quoted and sourced) plus a format scan citing real numbers
steps.check: every objection has a quoted source and a date; every 'format working now' line cites a real metric, not an impression
steps.ask_founder_if: no support inbox or review source is connected for this brand

steps.name: Pull competitor signal for layout and mood
steps.does: Pulls 3 to 8 competitor ad references from the Meta gallery's Competitors tab and the Reference Scout, tagged with why each fits this bottleneck.
steps.output: 3 to 8 tagged competitor references, layout and mood only
steps.check: every reference carries a one-line reason and a 'signal only' tag; no text, logo, product or face is marked for reuse

steps.name: Define the angle and dominant appeal
steps.does: Turns the objection map, format scan and avatar into 2 to 4 candidate angles, each one sentence, one persona, one dominant appeal, one buying question.
steps.output: angle brief: 2 to 4 angles, each with persona, appeal, buying question, awareness stage
steps.check: no angle uses a forbidden-tier claim; each angle names one dominant appeal only

steps.name: Write the test plan
steps.does: Turns the angle brief into a hypothesis, a clean one-persona-per-ad-set structure, a pack size sized to the account's own delivery volume, and a pre-set winner and kill rule for the creative side.
inputs: registry: past test sizes for this brand
steps.output: test brief: hypothesis, pack size, winner rule, kill rule, minimum read window
steps.check: winner and kill rule exist before any script is written; pack size matches this account's real traffic, not a generic default

steps.name: Build the audience spec and hand it to MEDIA
steps.does: Turns the angle's persona into age range, traits, interests and exclusions matched to the avatar record, and hands the spec to the Media buyer specialist as a structured request. CREA does not build or launch the audience itself.
steps.output: audience spec record: age range, traits, exclusions, matched persona id, handed to MEDIA
steps.check: every trait in the spec ties back to a line in the persona record, not a guess
steps.ask_founder_if: the angle targets a persona with no avatar record yet

steps.name: Pick the format and compare format economics
steps.does: Chooses the ad format (static, native platform format, UGC video, founder video, carousel, catalogue) from the product's real education or demo need and the account's own expected profit per ad by format, not ROAS alone.
inputs: product facts: education or demo need
account's own cost-per-asset and format hit-rate history
steps.output: format decision with the profit-per-ad comparison behind it
steps.check: decision cites a number, not a preference

steps.name: Write hooks and scripts or copy per format
steps.does: Writes the hook bank (8 to 20 hooks, graded on 5 criteria) and the format-specific script or static copy structure for each chosen format.
steps.output: hook bank plus a script or copy draft per format
steps.check: no product name or offer in a cold hook; one dominant appeal held throughout

steps.name: Build the creative brief and production or shoot brief
steps.does: Fills the one-page concept brief, then the format-specific production brief (static design brief, UGC or founder-video brief, or catalogue template spec) and generates a first draft image where the format calls for one.
steps.output: concept brief, production brief, and a draft asset (image or script package)
steps.check: destination link matches the offer stated; hook, image and copy share one awareness stage; real product photo used if fit, material or scale matters

steps.name: Run the copy and claim-compliance pass
steps.does: Applies the fixed direct-response copywriting rules (reading level, single idea, proof ranking) and then the brand's claim-tier and platform-policy check on every line.
steps.output: edited copy plus a claim audit table, pass or fail per line
steps.check: reading level under grade 10; no claim from the forbidden tier; no em dash
steps.ask_founder_if: a claim sits at the edge of the site-backed tier

steps.name: Run a feedback and reference round with the Reference Scout
steps.does: Sends the draft brief and asset back through one reference round: checks it against the tagged competitor references for layout and mood fit, and routes it for one internal feedback pass before it reaches a human reviewer.
inputs: past founder feedback notes if any
steps.output: revised brief or asset with a short note on what changed and why
steps.check: no competitor text, logo, product or face was copied in the revision

steps.name: Apply naming and tagging
steps.does: Applies the fixed naming and tagging schema (concept, persona, angle, offer, format, stage, source) to every asset and copy file before it leaves CREA.
steps.check: every asset has a stable id following the current schema

steps.name: Build the launch checklist and hand off to MEDIA
steps.does: Assembles the launch checklist (creative files, copy, audience spec reference, test brief, destination link, tracking check) and hands the full package to the Media buyer specialist for account build and go-live.
steps.output: launch checklist and handoff package to MEDIA
steps.check: every checklist line is checked or has a named blocker; MEDIA confirms receipt

steps.name: Read the first-read numbers
steps.does: At the test brief's minimum read window, pulls the creative-side metrics (hook rate, hold rate, CPA per ad) from the metric contract and compares each ad to the account average and the test's pre-set winner and kill rule.
inputs: metric contract fields at the read window
test brief's winner and kill rule
steps.output: read note: winner, loser or inconclusive, per ad, against the pre-set rule
steps.check: verdict uses the pre-set rule, not a new judgment call; missing metrics show as unavailable, never zero

steps.name: Log the result and close the loop
steps.does: Writes the registry entry for this test (angle, format, hook, result, learning) so the next research pass in step 1 starts from it.
steps.check: entry links back to the original card or idea id

qa: every claim traced to an approved or site-backed tier
no competitor text, logo, product or face reused
reading level under grade 10
real product photo used where accuracy matters
winner and kill rule set before launch
every number came from the metric contract, not estimated
read_point: at the test brief's minimum read window (set in step 4 from the account's own delivery volume, not a fixed default)
typical_duration: agent time: half a day to a day across the pipeline; waiting time: the read window itself, typically 3 to 10 days depending on account volume
subagents: Creative Studio Operator: step 8 image variant generation
Creative Performance Analyst: step 13 read, if a full teardown is warranted

name: Script a founder or authority-led ad
human_role: Direct-response scriptwriter briefing a founder or authority-led ad
inputs_required: brand brain: founder's real stories, credentials and permissioned reviews

steps.name: Confirm the founder fact set
steps.does: Pulls the founder's or authority's real, permissioned stories, credentials and reviews from the brand brain. Nothing invented.
inputs: brand brain: founder bio and story log
steps.check: every fact in the sheet has a source and a date on file
steps.ask_founder_if: a strong story exists but no written permission is on file

steps.name: Pick the argument, not a biography
steps.does: Frames the ad as an argument for the viewer's problem (claim, proof, mechanism), never a life story, using the angle brief.
steps.check: outline states the viewer's problem in the first line, not the founder's history

steps.name: Write the script skeleton
steps.does: Drafts the scene-by-scene script (hook, bridge, mechanism, product, proof, objection, CTA) sized to the product's real education need.
steps.check: single CTA; no unverified claim

steps.name: Diversify the founder's own sourcing
steps.does: Varies delivery style, setting and specific proof point across 2 to 3 script variants so the same founder does not read as one repeated ad.
steps.check: each variant uses a different real proof point, not a reworded line

steps.name: Direct the shoot or AI-touched frame
steps.does: Sets shot direction (gaze toward the CTA, setting, product visibility) for a real shoot or an AI-touched frame, keeping the founder's real likeness accurate.
steps.check: founder's real face and product are not redrawn

steps.name: Run the copy and claim pass
steps.does: Applies copywriting rules then the claim-tier check on every spoken and on-screen line.
steps.check: no claim outside the approved or site-backed tier

steps.name: Clear rights and hand off
steps.does: Confirms any stock element (music, b-roll) used alongside the founder footage is cleared, then hands the finished script package to production or the shoot workflow.
steps.check: every non-founder asset in the script has a license on file

qa: no invented founder story
no claim outside approved tiers
single CTA per script
read_point: same read window as the launch workflow once the script ships as an ad
typical_duration: agent time: 2 to 3 hours; waiting time: none until a shoot is booked

name: Brief and source a UGC creator, track rights
human_role: Creator brief writer and UGC rights tracker
inputs_required: past creator work and vetting notes

steps.name: Scan organic mentions for ad-worthy content
steps.does: Scans the brand's own tags, mentions and review videos for genuine customer content strong enough to become a paid ad.
steps.output: shortlist of candidate organic clips with source and date
steps.check: each clip traces to a real public post, not a screenshot with no source
steps.ask_founder_if: no social listening source is connected

steps.name: Vet the shortlist
steps.does: Checks each candidate against the vetting bar set by past creator work: authenticity, product visibility, tone match.
steps.check: every kept clip scores above the bar on all three criteria

steps.name: Decide wide or specific brief
steps.does: Picks a wide, discovery-style brief for a new creator or a specific, replication-style brief when a proven structure already exists.
steps.check: decision states why, not just a default

steps.name: Write the creator brief
steps.does: Writes the concept, the do and don't say list, and the take allowance. Never sends a creator to 'make content' with no concept.
steps.check: brief names a concept and a specific do/don't list

steps.name: Set usage rights and expiry
steps.does: Sets the rights scope (paid whitelisting versus organic only), duration and renewal date before any paid use.
steps.output: rights terms attached to the brief
steps.check: expiry date is set and logged before any spend touches this content
steps.ask_founder_if: a creator's ask sits outside the brand's standard rights terms

steps.name: Log to the rights tracker
steps.does: Writes the rights log entry: creator, content id, scope, expiry, renewal contact.
steps.check: entry appears in the tracker before the content ships as a paid ad

steps.name: Flag expiring rights weekly
steps.does: On the weekly run, checks the tracker for anything expiring inside 30 days and flags it before a whitelisted post silently reverts to organic-only.
steps.check: every flag reaches a person before the expiry date

qa: no UGC used without a concept brief
no paid use without a logged rights expiry date
read_point: first-read window once the sourced or briefed content runs as an ad, per CREA-W01
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours per creator; weekly scan: 30 minutes

name: Direct a product photo or video shoot
human_role: Creative producer running a shoot to spec
inputs_required: approved creative or concept brief needing real photography
product facts: real dimensions, material, color, fit

steps.name: Set image-accuracy direction
steps.does: Sets direction so the product shown will match what arrives at home: real color, scale next to a known object, material texture visible.
steps.check: brief names the exact product variant or SKU being shot, not a generic stand-in

steps.name: Build the shot list
steps.does: Turns the brief into a numbered shot list, with angles and gaze direction toward the CTA when a person is in frame.
steps.check: every shot ties to a specific ad or page use, not a generic library

steps.name: Book studio or location and model
steps.does: Books the shoot slot, studio or location, and any model, from the approved production budget line.
steps.check: booking sits inside the monthly production budget from CREA-W09 or CREA-W10
steps.ask_founder_if: the shoot needs a budget line not yet approved

steps.name: Get signed releases
steps.does: Collects the signed model and location release before the shoot starts, never after.
steps.check: release is on file before a single frame is used in any draft

steps.name: Run the shoot against the shot list
steps.does: A person runs the shoot; CREA checks each delivered frame against the shot list and the image-accuracy brief as it comes in.
steps.output: raw frame set checked against the shot list
steps.check: every shot list line has a matching delivered frame or a named gap

steps.name: Retouch QA against the real product
steps.does: Checks that retouching does not alter the real product's color, fit, scale or material past what a customer will actually receive.
steps.check: no retouch changes a fact-bearing detail: size, color or material

steps.name: File to the asset library
steps.does: Names, tags and files the final frames using the standing naming schema.
steps.check: every frame has a stable id and a release on file before it is usable downstream

qa: release on file before use
no retouch misrepresents the real product
read_point: not applicable directly; frames feed CREA-W01's assets and are read at that workflow's read point
typical_duration: agent time: 2 to 4 hours of briefing and QA; waiting time: the shoot day plus retouch turnaround, 3 to 7 days

name: Turn a live product page into a fast first-pass ad variant set
human_role: Fast-turn creative drafter for a new or under-tested SKU

steps.name: Read the live page
steps.does: Reads the live product page and pulls its images, price and stated claims exactly as shown.
steps.output: page facts: images, price, stated claims
steps.check: every claim pulled matches the page's exact wording, nothing added

steps.name: Cross-check claims against the brand record
steps.does: Matches each pulled claim to the brand's claim tiers and drops anything the page states that is not on record.
steps.check: no claim survives that is not in the approved or site-backed tier

steps.name: Draft first-pass static variants
steps.does: Drafts 3 to 5 static ad variants pairing the real page images with headline options built from the cleared claims.
steps.check: product image is the real photo from the page, not redrawn

steps.name: Draft a first-pass video or UGC concept
steps.does: Drafts one short video or UGC concept using the same cleared claims, as a second format option.
steps.check: concept states the same claims as the static set, no drift

steps.name: Write headline and primary-text sets
steps.does: Writes headline and primary-text variant sets for the static drafts, checked against length and image fit.
steps.check: each headline fits the platform's current character limit

steps.name: Run the copy pass
steps.does: Applies the core copywriting rules (reading level, single idea) to the full first-pass set.
steps.check: reading level under grade 10

steps.name: Hand off as a fast-test candidate
steps.does: Packages the first-pass set as a candidate for CREA-W01's test-plan step, flagged as unproven and needing its own read.
steps.check: package is clearly flagged as first-pass, not a finished concept

qa: no claim beyond the page's own claim-tier match
real product photo used
read_point: feeds into CREA-W01's test plan and read point once launched
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours
subagents: Creative Studio Operator: step 3 image variant generation

name: Localise a creative and copy set for a new market or device
human_role: Localisation editor for a target market and device
inputs_required: target market's payment, delivery and trust facts

steps.name: Confirm the target spec
steps.does: Confirms the device target (mobile-first, vertical-only formats where the target market's traffic calls for it) and market facts (payment method mix, delivery windows, local payment logos; COD availability and EMI where the target market runs them, markets: IN) for the target market.
steps.check: every trust fact on the sheet matches the current brand policy, not an assumption
steps.ask_founder_if: the brand has no policy on file for this market yet

steps.name: Re-cut for vertical, mobile-first delivery
steps.does: Re-crops or re-composes the framing for vertical, mobile-first delivery, and flags any asset that cannot be honestly re-cropped.
steps.check: no important element is cropped out of frame

steps.name: Localise the copy
steps.does: Rewrites hooks and copy for the local reading level and, where needed, drafts a dual-language hook pairing that matches how the persona actually speaks.
steps.check: dual-language line reads as a natural code-switch, not a literal translation

steps.name: Swap in local trust facts
steps.does: Replaces any non-local trust line (a foreign currency guarantee, a foreign shipping time) with the real local fact: payment method mix, local return window, local payment logos; COD availability where the target market runs it, markets: IN.
steps.check: every trust fact traces to the current local policy record

steps.name: Run the compliance pass
steps.does: Runs the claim and copywriting-rules check on the localised set.
steps.check: no claim carried over that does not hold in the local market

steps.name: Hand off as a market-tagged variant
steps.does: Tags the finished set with the market and device so it never runs against the wrong audience.
steps.check: every asset carries a market tag before handoff

qa: no non-local trust claim survives
dual-language line reads natural
read_point: same read point as the parent test once launched in-market
typical_duration: agent time: 2 to 3 hours per market

name: Diagnose creative fatigue and brief the revival
human_role: Creative performance analyst watching for wear-out
inputs_required: lifecycle metrics: days to fatigue, frequency
hook bank for the fatigued ad's angle

steps.name: Pull lifecycle metrics
steps.does: Pulls each live ad's frequency, hold rate and CPA trend against the account's own historical fatigue curve.
inputs: metric contract: frequency, hold rate, cpa trend
steps.check: every candidate compares to this account's own curve, not a generic industry number

steps.name: Rule out a small-audience-pool cause
steps.does: Checks delivery volume and frequency to see if the drop is really audience exhaustion, not creative wear-out.
steps.check: verdict names the specific number that decided it

steps.name: Diagnose the creative cause
steps.does: For creative-caused fatigue, identifies which part wore out: hook, visual, or the whole concept.
steps.check: diagnosis names one specific part, not a general 'the ad is tired'

steps.name: Prescribe the cheapest real fix first
steps.does: Proposes a hook swap or format rotation before a whole new concept, in that order, using the existing hook bank.
steps.check: brief tries the cheapest fix first unless the diagnosis rules it out

steps.name: Route audience-pool cases to MEDIA
steps.does: For audience-pool causes, hands the finding to MEDIA instead of commissioning new creative.
steps.check: note is explicit that this is not a creative problem

steps.name: Log the fatigue event
steps.does: Writes the registry entry for the fatigue event and its prescribed fix, feeding CREA-W08's teardown history.
steps.check: entry links the original ad id to the fix tried

qa: diagnosis names a specific metric and comparison, not a guess
read_point: weekly, against the account's rolling fatigue curve
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour per week across the live set
subagents: Creative Performance Analyst: full weekly scan

name: Tear down the week's winners and losers
human_role: Creative analyst writing the weekly breakdown
inputs_required: ad creative (image or video) and copy

steps.name: Pull the week's ad-level results
steps.does: Pulls every ad's metrics next to the account average for the same period.
steps.output: ranked ad list for the week
steps.check: totals and per-ad breakdowns are kept separate, never summed into one number

steps.name: Break each ad into its parts
steps.does: For the top and bottom ads, breaks the creative into hook, structure, proof, offer and CTA.
steps.check: every part is named, none skipped

steps.name: Write the hypothesis per ad
steps.does: Writes a specific hypothesis for why each ad worked or did not, backed by the number that shows it.
steps.check: hypothesis cites a number, not an opinion

steps.name: Check against competitor signal
steps.does: Notes whether a winning structure echoes a competitor pattern already tagged as signal, without claiming causation.
steps.check: note is marked signal only, never proof

steps.name: Assign a funnel role
steps.does: From the real numbers, assigns each ad a funnel role: cold hook winner, retention proof, or bottom-funnel closer.
steps.check: tag matches the metric that drove it, for example high CTR with low CVR means top-funnel only

steps.name: Write the breakdown report
steps.does: Assembles the week's breakdown into a short report for the founder.
steps.check: report is under the founder's usual reading time; digits not spelled out

steps.name: Log the hypothesis
steps.does: Writes each hypothesis to the registry so future angle and hook work in CREA-W01 starts from it.
steps.check: each entry links to the ad id and the metric window used

qa: verdict backed by a specific number
competitor material marked signal only
read_point: weekly, on the last full day's data
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours

name: Plan the monthly creative production pipeline and portfolio mix
human_role: Creative producer planning next month's slate
inputs_required: current portfolio mix by angle, format and persona

steps.name: Pull the account's hit rate
steps.does: Pulls the real ratio of winning to tested creatives over the last quarter, by format and angle.
steps.output: hit-rate table by format and angle
steps.check: rate is computed in code from real results, not estimated

steps.name: Audit portfolio coverage
steps.does: Checks which persona, angle and format combinations are under-tested or over-concentrated.
steps.check: every active persona has at least one live test in the last 60 days, or is flagged

steps.name: Size next month's volume
steps.does: Sizes how many new concepts, variants and formats to produce next month from the hit rate and the budget line, not a fixed quota.
steps.check: plan's volume is derived from the hit rate and budget, shown as a calculation

steps.name: Sequence the pipeline stages
steps.does: Lays out the month across research, concept, build, variations, feedback and launch stages with dates.
steps.check: every stage has a date and an owner

steps.name: Flag budget risk early
steps.does: Cross-checks the planned volume against the cost-per-asset trend from CREA-W10 to flag a likely overrun before it happens.
steps.check: flag is raised before the month starts, not after an overrun

steps.name: Publish the plan
steps.does: Writes the plan up for the founder and MEDIA to see.
steps.check: plan is readable in one pass, digits not spelled out

qa: volume derived from hit rate and budget, not a guess
read_point: monthly, first business day of the month, on the prior full month's data
typical_duration: agent time: about 2 hours

name: Track production cost per asset against the monthly budget
inputs_required: real cost per asset produced: AI credits, freelancer or agency invoices, stock license fees

steps.name: Log real costs
steps.does: Logs every real cost as it is incurred, generation credits, invoices, license fees, against the specific asset it produced.
steps.check: every cost ties to a named asset id, never a lump sum

steps.name: Compute cost per asset
steps.does: Computes cost per finished asset by format, in code.
steps.check: computation is shown, not estimated

steps.name: Compare to the monthly plan
steps.does: Checks running spend against the monthly budget line from CREA-W09.
steps.check: status shows unavailable, not zero, for any cost not yet logged

steps.name: Flag a likely overrun
steps.does: If the trend line crosses the budget before month end, flags it to the founder with the number and the date it will cross.
steps.check: flag names the exact projected crossing date
steps.ask_founder_if: the projected overrun exceeds 15% of the monthly line

steps.name: Log to the registry
steps.does: Writes the weekly cost snapshot to the registry for the next monthly plan.
steps.check: entry is dated and links to the current monthly plan

qa: every cost tied to a named asset
missing cost shown as unavailable, never zero
read_point: weekly, on real invoices and credit usage logged that week
typical_duration: agent time: 30 to 45 minutes

name: Maintain the naming, tagging and platform-spec standard
human_role: Creative operations owner of the naming standard
inputs_required: each ad platform's current character and spec limits

steps.name: Audit the current schema against real assets
steps.does: Checks a sample of recent assets against the standing naming and tagging schema for drift.
steps.check: every drift instance is named, not just counted

steps.name: Refresh the platform spec sheet
steps.does: Re-checks each ad platform's current character limits, aspect ratios and file-size caps, since these change without notice.
steps.check: sheet's last-checked date is under 30 days when copy is being written to a limit

steps.name: Update the schema if needed
steps.does: Adjusts the schema for a new format, persona or offer type added since the last check.
steps.check: update does not break the id stability of existing assets

steps.name: Re-tag drifted assets
steps.does: Fixes tags on any asset found off-schema in the audit.
steps.check: every drifted asset now matches the current schema

steps.name: Publish the standard
steps.does: Writes the current schema and spec sheet to a place every CREA workflow reads from.
steps.check: publish date is visible to every workflow that reads it

qa: spec sheet checked within 30 days when in active use
read_point: monthly
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour

name: Set and update where AI may be used in the pipeline
human_role: AI-use governance owner for the creative pipeline
inputs_required: any new AI tool or capability entering the pipeline

steps.name: List where AI touches the pipeline
steps.does: Lists every point AI drafts, generates or grades something across CREA's workflows.
steps.check: map covers every workflow, none skipped

steps.name: Classify each touchpoint
steps.does: Classifies each touchpoint as drafting or grunt work, allowed unsupervised, or final ideation and authorship, never unsupervised.
steps.check: no final-ideation touchpoint is marked unsupervised

steps.name: Ground each AI draft in brand facts
steps.does: Confirms each drafting touchpoint is fed the brand's own facts (claim tiers, voice, product data), not generic training knowledge.
steps.check: every drafting step names its brand-fact input

steps.name: Update the policy for a new tool
steps.does: When a new AI capability enters the pipeline, for example an AI-actor or voice-clone tool, classifies it and adds it to the policy before use.
steps.check: policy update happens before the tool's first real use
steps.ask_founder_if: a new tool would touch final ideation or unsupervised authorship

steps.name: Publish and log the policy
steps.does: Publishes the current policy and logs the update.
steps.check: policy is dated and visible to every CREA workflow

qa: no final-ideation step runs unsupervised
every AI draft grounded in brand facts
read_point: continuous, reviewed at every new tool or quarterly, whichever comes first
typical_duration: agent time: ongoing, about 30 minutes per review

name: Frame a price or offer's value in copy
inputs_required: the specific price or offer to frame

steps.name: Pull the real price and policy facts
steps.does: Pulls the exact price, any discount, and the policy limits ops can honor, from the brand brain.
steps.check: every number matches the current live price, not a cached one

steps.name: Choose the ending style
steps.does: Picks a charm ending (.99/.95) or a round-number ending based on the brand's positioning: value versus premium.
steps.check: decision matches the stated positioning, not a default

steps.name: Build the cost-per-day reframe if it helps
steps.does: Builds a cost-per-day or cost-per-use reframe when it makes the price feel smaller honestly.
steps.check: the math behind the reframe is shown and correct

steps.name: State the honest reason for a low price
steps.does: If the price looks unusually low, writes the real reason, for example clearance, factory-direct, or a holiday sale, rather than leaving it unexplained.
steps.check: reason is a real, checkable fact, not a manufactured urgency

steps.name: Check the guarantee wording
steps.does: Matches any guarantee or urgency line exactly to what ops can honor.
steps.check: wording matches ops eligibility exactly, no rounding up
steps.ask_founder_if: the requested wording exceeds what ops confirmed it can honor

steps.name: Run the claim pass
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check on the finished price copy block.
steps.check: no claim beyond the approved or site-backed tier

qa: guarantee wording matches ops exactly
no fabricated deadline
read_point: read at whichever ad or page workflow requested it
typical_duration: agent time: 30 to 45 minutes

name: Name a new product or proprietary system
inputs_required: the benefit or story it should carry

steps.name: Pull the benefit to carry
steps.does: Pulls the single strongest benefit or mechanism the name should carry, from the product facts and the angle brief if one exists.
steps.check: benefit is one sentence, one idea

steps.name: Draft name candidates
steps.does: Drafts 8 to 15 name candidates that carry the benefit or attach to a real named person.
steps.check: every candidate ties to the benefit statement, not a generic-sounding word

steps.name: Check for real-person attachment
steps.does: If a real named person, for example the founder or a formulator, is attached, confirms the story is real and permissioned.
steps.check: no invented person or credential
steps.ask_founder_if: a candidate implies a credential not on file

steps.name: Screen for conflicts
steps.does: Screens candidates for an obvious trademark or marketplace-listing conflict via public search.
steps.check: shortlist notes any close public match found

steps.name: Rank and present to the founder
steps.does: Ranks the shortlist against the benefit fit and presents it as a founder_gate decision.
steps.check: ranking states the reason for the order
steps.ask_founder_if: always, naming is founder_gate

qa: no invented credential or story
read_point: not applicable; the decision happens at the founder gate
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour

name: Refresh objection-handling and retargeting continuity copy
inputs_required: customer data source: support tickets, reviews, return reasons

steps.name: Pull real objections from customer data
steps.does: Pulls the most common real objections from support tickets, reviews and return reasons, ranked by frequency.
steps.output: ranked objection list with quoted sources
steps.check: every objection has a real quoted source and a count
steps.ask_founder_if: no support or returns data source is connected

steps.name: Write one line per objection
steps.does: Writes one bottom-funnel ad line or copy block per objection, prefacing the most common one early rather than saving it for an FAQ.
steps.check: the top-ranked objection is addressed in the first line, not buried

steps.name: Keep the sequence consistent
steps.does: Checks the new lines against the existing retargeting sequence so the same objection is not answered twice with contradicting facts.
steps.check: no two steps in the sequence contradict each other

steps.name: Run the claim pass
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check on every objection response, since these often brush against guarantee or comparison claims.
steps.check: no forbidden-tier claim used to defuse an objection

steps.name: Hand off to the owning surface
steps.does: Hands the finished lines to whichever surface will run them: an ad via CREA-W01, or an email or SMS block via Lifecycle.
steps.check: handoff names the exact surface and owner

qa: every objection traced to a real quoted source
top objection addressed first, not last
read_point: at the read point of whichever surface deploys the copy
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours

name: Write payment and delivery reassurance creative messaging
inputs_required: current payment method mix and failed/reversed-order rates (chargeback_rate, return_to_sender_rate; cod_share and rto_rate where the brand runs COD, markets: IN)
reassurance incentive if any (BNPL, free returns, discount); prepaid incentive if the brand runs COD (markets: IN)
delivery-trust facts: carrier, timelines, tracking, ID verification where COD applies

steps.name: Pull the real payment-mix and reversed-order numbers
steps.does: Pulls the account's current payment method mix and failed/reversed-order rates (chargeback_rate, return_to_sender_rate) to size how much this messaging matters right now; for a COD brand, also pulls cod_share and rto_rate.
inputs: metric contract: payment_method_mix, chargeback_rate, return_to_sender_rate, cod_share, rto_rate (cod_share and rto_rate read null outside markets: IN)
steps.check: numbers pulled from the metric contract, not estimated

steps.name: Write the payment reassurance line
steps.does: Writes the ad and checkout line that removes payment friction: a BNPL option, card or wallet trust fact, or, for a COD brand, the prepaid nudge (discount, faster dispatch), honest and specific.
steps.check: any discount, BNPL or speed claim matches what ops actually offers

steps.name: Write the delivery-trust messaging
steps.does: Writes the trust lines that lower failed-delivery and return-to-sender risk: real carrier name, real delivery window, tracking fact; for a COD brand, the same lines also lower return-to-origin (RTO) risk.
steps.check: every fact matches current ops policy, not an aspiration

steps.name: Run the claim pass
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check, since delivery-time, BNPL and discount claims are a common source of drift.
steps.check: no delivery-time claim beyond the current real average

steps.name: Hand off with the baseline attached
steps.does: Hands the copy to MEDIA or the Site specialist with the payment-mix and reversed-order baseline attached so impact can be measured later.
steps.check: baseline numbers travel with the copy

qa: every delivery, BNPL or discount fact matches current ops policy
read_point: next full month's payment method mix and reversed-order rates after deployment
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour

name: Build Amazon A+ Content and marketplace brand-store modules
inputs_required: marketplace's current module template grid: Amazon A+, Walmart Marketplace or Target Plus brand shop; Flipkart or Myntra brand store for an India-market brand (markets: IN)

steps.name: Pull the current template grid
steps.does: Pulls the marketplace's own current A+ Content or brand-store module system, since these are fixed and change per platform update.
steps.check: spec checked within the last 30 days

steps.name: Pick the modules for this product
steps.does: Picks the banner, infographic and comparison-chart modules that fit this product's real differentiators.
steps.check: every module chosen has content to fill it, not a placeholder

steps.name: Write the module copy
steps.does: Writes the copy for each module within its exact character and layout limits.
steps.check: copy fits each module's real space, no overflow

steps.name: Direct the module imagery
steps.does: Directs the real product photo or diagram used in each visual module, no product redraw where fit or scale is the point.
steps.check: real product photo used for every fit or scale claim

steps.name: Run the claim pass
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check on every comparison-chart line especially, since these draw the most marketplace policy scrutiny.
steps.check: no comparison claim without evidence on file

steps.name: Hand off to Product and Supply
steps.does: Hands the finished modules to the Product and Supply specialist, who owns the actual marketplace listing surface.
steps.check: package includes the exact module grid slot for each piece

qa: module grid spec checked within 30 days
real photo used for fit or scale claims
read_point: next full month's listing conversion rate after publish, read by Product and Supply
typical_duration: agent time: 2 to 3 hours

name: Build and maintain an AI character or mascot sheet

steps.name: Define the character's fixed traits
steps.does: Fixes the character's core traits so the identity does not drift across generations.
steps.check: every trait is specific enough to reject a wrong regeneration

steps.name: Generate the reference sheet
steps.does: Generates the fixed set of expressions, angles and outfit views used as the anchor for every future generation.
steps.check: sheet covers the angles and expressions the pipeline actually reuses

steps.name: File and version the sheet
steps.does: Names, tags and versions the reference sheet so every later generation cites the exact version used.
steps.check: version id is stable and referenced by every downstream asset

steps.name: Check each new use against the sheet
steps.does: Before any new asset uses the character, checks it against the current reference sheet for identity drift.
steps.check: any drift is caught before the asset ships

steps.name: Update the sheet on a real change
steps.does: When the founder approves a real change, for example a new outfit or expression, updates the sheet as a new version rather than editing history.
steps.check: old version stays on file, not overwritten

qa: no identity drift ships uncaught
read_point: not applicable directly; feeds whichever creative uses the character
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours to build, 15 minutes per reuse check

name: Generate a synthetic AI-actor UGC video ad
inputs_required: founder approval to use a synthetic actor for this test

steps.name: Confirm the founder gate
steps.does: Confirms the founder has approved using a licensed AI actor for this specific test before generating anything.
steps.check: approval is on record for this specific use, not a standing blanket approval
steps.ask_founder_if: no approval is on file yet

steps.name: Finalize the script for a synthetic read
steps.does: Finalizes the hook-to-camera script, since a synthetic actor reads exactly what is written with no ad lib.
steps.check: script contains no line that needs natural ad lib to land

steps.name: Run the claim pass
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check before generation, since a synthetic ad cannot be caught and reshot the way a human one can.
steps.check: no unverified claim reaches generation

steps.name: Generate the AI-actor video
steps.does: Generates the finished vertical video using the licensed AI actor reading the audited script.
steps.check: actor's on-screen claims match the audited script exactly, no drift from generation

steps.name: Caption and QA
steps.does: Adds burned-in captions and checks the finished video against the QA checklist before it counts as ready.
steps.check: captions match the spoken line exactly

steps.name: Flag it as synthetic in the handoff
steps.does: Flags the asset as AI-actor generated in its metadata and handoff note, for platform disclosure rules and internal tracking.
steps.check: disclosure tag is present before handoff to MEDIA

qa: founder approval on file before generation
no unverified claim in the read
read_point: same read point as CREA-W01 once launched as a test
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour plus generation wait, typically 10 to 30 minutes

name: Clone a consenting voice for voiceover variants
trigger: on demand, founder_gate, only after consent is on file
inputs_required: documented written consent from the founder or contracted creator

steps.name: Confirm written consent is on file
steps.does: Confirms the specific person's documented written consent is on file for voice cloning before doing anything else.
steps.check: consent document is dated, named and specific to this use
steps.ask_founder_if: consent is missing, expired, or does not cover this specific use

steps.name: Prepare the voice model
steps.does: Prepares the cloned voice model from the consented source recording.
steps.check: model is built only from the consented recording

steps.name: Generate the script variant reads
steps.does: Generates voiceover for each approved script variant using the cloned voice.
steps.check: each variant reads the exact audited script line

steps.name: QA against the real person's cadence
steps.does: Checks the generated read against the real person's known cadence and pronunciation for anything that would sound obviously wrong.
steps.check: no line mispronounces a name or term the real person would say correctly

steps.name: Tag and log the use
steps.does: Tags every generated line with the consent record id and logs the use so consent scope is never exceeded.
steps.check: log entry shows total uses against any use-count limit in the consent

qa: consent on file before any generation
use logged against any consent limit
read_point: same read point as the ad workflow that uses the voiceover
typical_duration: agent time: about 1 hour plus generation wait

name: Score a creative batch before it enters paid testing
trigger: event: before a new batch enters paid testing
inputs_required: the account's own past predictive-score-to-outcome record, if any

steps.name: Run the predictive pass
steps.does: Runs each draft through the predictive scoring pass, flagging weak elements.
steps.output: predicted score per draft, per element
steps.check: score names the specific element flagged, hook clarity, headline-image mismatch or CTA visibility, not just an overall number

steps.name: Compare to this account's own history
steps.does: Checks whether this account's past predictive scores actually tracked real outcomes, and downweights the score if not.
steps.check: calibration is shown, not assumed accurate

steps.name: Flag weak elements for a fix
steps.does: Sends any draft with a flagged weak element back for a specific fix, not a general redo.
steps.check: fix list names the exact element, not 'make it better'

steps.name: Re-score after fix
steps.does: Re-runs the pass on fixed drafts before clearing them for test.
steps.check: post-fix score is logged next to the original for calibration tracking

steps.name: Clear the batch
steps.does: Clears the batch for CREA-W01's launch checklist once every draft passes or has a named, accepted risk.
steps.check: every draft is either passed or has a named, founder-accepted risk
steps.ask_founder_if: a draft fails but the founder wants to test it anyway

qa: score calibrated against this account's real outcomes, not assumed
read_point: the batch's actual paid-test read point, used to recalibrate the scorer over time
typical_duration: agent time: 30 to 45 minutes per batch

name: Resize, caption and cut one master creative into every derivative
inputs_required: the platform placement list it needs to cover

steps.name: List the required placements
steps.does: Lists every aspect-ratio and placement version the platform set needs: feed square, story vertical, in-stream widescreen.
steps.check: list matches the current, not stale, platform-spec sheet

steps.name: Recompose, don't just crop
steps.does: Recomposes the master for each placement, repositioning subject and text rather than a blind crop, so nothing important is lost.
steps.check: no important element, CTA, product or face, is cropped out in any version

steps.name: Cut length derivatives
steps.does: If the master is long-form video, cuts a 15-second and a 6-second bumper version, each keyed to a different hook from the hook bank.
steps.check: each cut opens on a distinct hook, not the same first 6 seconds repeated

steps.name: Burn in captions
steps.does: Adds accurate burned-in captions to every video version, since most are watched muted.
steps.check: captions match the spoken line exactly, correctly timed

steps.name: Write alt text
steps.does: Writes descriptive alt text for every static image version.
steps.check: alt text describes what is actually shown, not the ad's selling line

steps.name: QA the full derivative set
steps.does: Checks every derivative against the master for message-match drift before it ships.
steps.check: every derivative says the same thing as the master, no drift

steps.name: Name, tag and hand off
steps.does: Names and tags every derivative under the standing schema and hands the full set to the launch checklist.
steps.check: every derivative has a stable id before handoff

qa: no important element cropped out
captions accurate and correctly timed
no message-match drift across derivatives
read_point: each derivative reads at its own placement's read point inside CREA-W01
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours per master

name: Clear stock footage, fonts and music rights before a video ships
trigger: event: before a video ad using licensed assets ships
inputs_required: every licensed stock footage, font and music asset used in the video

steps.name: List every licensed asset used
steps.does: Lists every piece of stock footage, font and music track used in the finished video.
steps.check: list is exhaustive, cross-checked against the actual timeline, not memory

steps.name: Pull each asset's real license terms
steps.does: Pulls the actual license terms for each asset: commercial use, territory, term length, exclusivity.
steps.check: terms are the actual document, not a remembered summary

steps.name: Match use to terms
steps.does: Checks the video's actual use, paid ad, territory, duration of the campaign, against each license's real limits.
steps.output: match or mismatch result per asset
steps.check: every asset gets a clear pass or a named mismatch

steps.name: Fix or swap a mismatch
steps.does: Swaps out any asset whose license does not cover this use, before the video ships.
steps.check: no mismatched asset remains in the final video
steps.ask_founder_if: a needed asset has no compliant replacement and the founder must decide to reshoot, re-license or drop it

steps.name: Log the clearance
steps.does: Logs the clearance record for each asset so a later renewal or takedown risk can be tracked.
steps.check: log entry includes each license's expiry or renewal date

qa: every asset in the final video has a matching, logged license
read_point: not applicable directly; a compliance gate before CREA-W01's launch checklist
typical_duration: agent time: 30 to 60 minutes per video

name: Build catalogue-scale ad variants and DPA overlay templates from the feed
trigger: event: new catalogue campaign, or on feed refresh
human_role: Catalogue and DPA creative template builder
inputs_required: current product feed: price, image, SKU fields
a small set of approved copy blocks

steps.name: Audit the feed for dirty data
steps.does: Checks the feed's price and image fields for gaps, wrong formats or stale data before building anything on top of it.
steps.check: audit flags every SKU with a missing or malformed required field
steps.ask_founder_if: more than a set share of SKUs fail the audit

steps.name: Design the overlay template
steps.does: Designs the price, discount and badge overlay template so it renders correctly across every SKU's real image dimensions and price-string length.
steps.check: template is tested against the longest real price string and the smallest real product image in the feed

steps.name: Write the copy block set
steps.does: Writes a small set of reusable copy blocks, headline and primary-text patterns, that plug into any SKU's feed fields.
steps.check: every block reads correctly with a real, varied sample of SKU data plugged in

steps.name: Generate the full variant grid
steps.does: Combines the template, the feed's fields and the copy blocks to produce the full grid of ad variants across every SKU.
steps.check: spot-check a random sample of SKUs for correct price, image and copy pairing

steps.name: Flag catalogue and DPA risk
steps.does: Flags anything that will break at scale: a badge that overlaps a price string on a particular SKU, a missing image, a discontinued item still live.
steps.check: every flagged risk names the specific SKU

steps.name: Run the claim pass on the copy blocks
steps.does: Runs the claim-tier check once on the reusable copy blocks, since they apply across the whole grid.
steps.check: no block claim outside the approved or site-backed tier

steps.name: Hand off to MEDIA and Product and Supply
steps.does: Hands the finished grid and the risk flag list to MEDIA for the DPA campaign build and to Product and Supply for feed fixes.
steps.check: every flagged risk has a named owner before handoff closes

qa: template tested against real longest and shortest feed values
every SKU-level risk named, not generalized
read_point: next full week's DPA performance after go-live, read by MEDIA
typical_duration: agent time: 2 to 4 hours for the first build, about 30 minutes on a routine feed refresh

name: Prepare the bulk upload sheet and hand off for draft-upload
trigger: event: creative batch approved for launch
inputs_required: approved batch of ad copy and creative filenames
the target platform's current bulk-upload or Ads Manager bulk-editor spec

steps.name: Confirm the batch is fully approved
steps.does: Confirms every item in the batch cleared CREA-W01's launch checklist before building the sheet.
steps.check: no item without a passed checklist enters the sheet

steps.name: Pull the current bulk-upload spec
steps.does: Pulls the exact column and format spec the target platform's bulk-upload tool or Ads Manager bulk editor currently expects.
steps.check: spec checked within 30 days

steps.name: Build the sheet, one row per ad
steps.does: Builds the exact spreadsheet or CSV, one row per ad, matching every required column.
steps.check: every row has every required column filled, no blank required field

steps.name: Spot-check against the creative brief
steps.does: Spot-checks a sample of rows against their original creative brief for a copy or filename mismatch.
steps.check: sample shows zero mismatches, or every mismatch is fixed before handoff

steps.name: Draft-upload as paused, unpublished
steps.does: Where the founder has approved it, drives Ads Manager's own web interface to create one paused, unpublished draft ad per approved creative, so a human reviews a real draft inside the platform before anything goes live.
steps.output: paused draft ads inside Ads Manager
steps.check: every created draft is confirmed paused and unpublished, never activated
steps.ask_founder_if: the browser-agent step has not yet been approved for this account

steps.name: Hand off to MEDIA for review and go-live
steps.does: Hands the sheet and the draft-ad list to MEDIA, who reviews each real draft and decides go-live.
steps.check: MEDIA confirms receipt of both the sheet and the draft list

outputs: paused draft ads inside Ads Manager
qa: no draft created ever gets activated by CREA
spec checked within 30 days
read_point: not applicable directly; read happens once MEDIA activates and CREA-W01's read point applies
typical_duration: agent time: 1 to 2 hours per batch
